en: change one's mind or attitude; turn over a new leaf

examples.ko: 저는 이런 기회에 백화점 구경도 해 두자고 마음을 고쳐먹었어요.
examples.en: I changed my mind and decided to take the chance to look around the department store too.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어진 뒤에 마음을 고쳐먹고 다시 공부를 시작했어요.
examples.en: After failing the exam, I changed my attitude and started studying again.
If you change your mind even now, it's not too late.
It isn't easy to change your mindset like that.
I'm really glad my friend had a change of heart.
Ever since I changed my attitude, I exercise every day.

explain: 주로 '마음, 생각, 버릇'을 목적어로 해서 먹었던 마음을 새로 바꾼다는 느낌으로 써요. '마음먹다'가 처음 결심하는 거라면 '고쳐먹다'는 다시 마음을 잡는 거예요. 주로 나쁜 쪽에서 좋은 쪽으로 바꿀 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used with objects like 마음 (mind), 생각 (thought) or 버릇 (habit), meaning to reset an attitude you had before. While '마음먹다' is making a decision for the first time, '고쳐먹다' is deciding again. It is often used for changing from a bad attitude to a better one.

examples.en: I don't want to disappoint my parents.
I disappointed my friend again.
I'm worried I'll disappoint my teacher by being late.
That concert did not disappoint the fans.

examples.ko: 기대하게 해 놓고 실망시키면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't get people's hopes up and then let them down.

examples.ko: 저를 믿어 준 사람들을 실망시킨 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never let down the people who trusted me.

explain: '실망하다'는 내가 실망할 때, '실망시키다'는 내가 다른 사람을 실망하게 만들 때 써요. '부모님을 실망시키다'처럼 '을/를'로 사람을 받아요. 죄송하다고 말할 때 '실망시켜서 죄송해요'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '실망하다' is when I am disappointed; '실망시키다' is when I make someone else disappointed. The person takes '을/를', as in '부모님을 실망시키다'. When apologizing you can say '실망시켜서 죄송해요'.

en: have a premonition; have a hunch

examples.ko: 아침부터 좋은 일이 생길 것 같다고 예감했어요.
examples.en: Since morning I had a feeling something good would happen.

examples.ko: 그는 시험에 떨어질 것을 예감하고 있었어요.
examples.en: He sensed that he would fail the exam.
When the phone rang, I sensed bad news.
I have a hunch that our team will win.

examples.ko: 어머니는 제가 올 줄 미리 예감하셨대요.
examples.en: My mother says she sensed ahead of time that I would come.

examples.ko: 비가 올 것을 예감하는 사람처럼 우산을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed an umbrella like someone who senses rain coming.

explain: '예감하다'는 이유 없이 마음으로 미리 느낄 때 써요. 근거를 들어 미리 맞히는 '예상하다', '예측하다'와 달라요. 그래서 '예감이 좋다/나쁘다'처럼 명사로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '예감하다' is for sensing something in advance with no clear reason. It differs from '예상하다' and '예측하다', which rely on evidence. People often use the noun form too, as in '예감이 좋다/나쁘다'.

examples.en: Don't hesitate like that, just say it quickly.
I didn't have the courage to confess, so I kept dithering.
I dawdled and missed the last bus.

examples.ko: 왜 질문에 대답도 못 하고 우물쭈물해요?
examples.en: Why are you hesitating instead of answering the question?
While I was dithering, all the seats got taken.

examples.ko: 메뉴를 못 골라서 직원 앞에서 우물쭈물하고 있었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't choose from the menu, so I was hesitating in front of the staff.

explain: '머뭇거리다'와 비슷하지만 '우물쭈물'은 말이나 행동을 분명하게 못 해서 답답해 보이는 느낌이 강해요. '우물쭈물 말을 얼버무리다'처럼 부사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '머뭇거리다' (to hesitate), but '우물쭈물' strongly suggests being unclear and indecisive in a frustrating way. It is also often used as an adverb, as in '우물쭈물 말을 얼버무리다' (to mumble evasively).

examples.en: When a child recognizes danger, he stops right away.
By the time I noticed the problem, it was already too late.
People perceive color first.

examples.ko: 자신의 감정을 인지하는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to be aware of your own feelings.

examples.ko: 회사는 사고 사실을 인지하고 조사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The company became aware of the accident and began an investigation.
I wasn't aware of that rule.

explain: '알다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 뉴스나 보고서에서 '문제를 인지하다'처럼 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '알아차리다', '깨닫다'가 더 자연스러워요. '인식하다'와 비슷한데, '인지하다'는 어떤 사실이 있다는 걸 아는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: A stiffer word than '알다', common in news and reports (e.g. '문제를 인지하다'). In daily talk, '알아차리다' or '깨닫다' sounds more natural. It is close to '인식하다', but '인지하다' stresses becoming aware that something exists.

examples.en: I failed the exam, but I didn't lose heart.
After failing again and again, he completely lost heart.

examples.ko: 좌절할 때마다 친구가 힘이 되어 줬어요.
examples.en: Every time I felt crushed, my friend supported me.
You shouldn't give up just because your dream hit a wall.

examples.ko: 좌절하는 모습이 안쓰러워서 따뜻하게 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: He looked so disheartened that I spoke to him kindly.

examples.ko: 저는 좌절하고 나서 오히려 더 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: After feeling defeated, I actually worked even harder.

explain: 좌절하다는 일이 뜻대로 안 돼서 의욕과 희망이 꺾인 상태예요. 슬프거나 화나는 감정보다 '이제 못하겠다'는 기운이 빠진 느낌에 가까워요. 위로할 때는 '좌절하지 마세요'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 좌절하다 describes losing motivation and hope because things did not go your way. It is less about sadness or anger and more about the drained feeling of 'I can't do this anymore'. A common phrase when comforting someone is '좌절하지 마세요'.

en: pull oneself together; compose oneself; hitch up

examples.en: I'll pull myself together and try again.
I need time to get myself back in shape.
The shock was big, so it was hard to collect myself.

examples.ko: 아픈 몸을 추스르는 동안 집에서 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I rested at home while recovering from being sick.

examples.ko: 슬픔을 추스르면 다시 일할 수 있을 거예요.
examples.en: Once you get over the sadness, you'll be able to work again.
I hitched up my bag strap and climbed the stairs.

explain: '마음, 몸, 정신'과 함께 써서 흐트러진 상태를 다시 가다듬는다는 느낌이 있어요. '정신을 차리다'보다 천천히 회복하는 느낌이 있고, 흘러내린 짐이나 옷을 위로 올릴 때도 써요. '추슬러요', '추슬렀어요'처럼 '르' 불규칙이니 주의해요.
explain_en: Used with '마음', '몸' and '정신', it feels like straightening yourself out after things got disordered. Compared with '정신을 차리다', it suggests a slower recovery, and it also works for hitching up a slipping bag or clothing. It is a '르' irregular verb, so it becomes '추슬러요' and '추슬렀어요'.
